items.text: “One sentence about a garden visit this week? Not what happened in it — just how the going was.”
“I went twice and it was quieter than Wednesday.” “I meant to and didn’t.” “I went once and it was hard.”
A parent offers the first sentence — never a cold call on a teen; each one received identically
“There is no junior varsity garden. Jesus meets each person in the garden they actually have.”
Same two anchors as last week — Psalm 23 and John 15:1–11 — “Listen as if for the first time anyway.”
A vinedresser does not visit a vine once — abiding is a rhythm, not an event
Going back changes things — the garden is not a photograph; it is a living place, because your heart is
A hard garden last week? Going back in tonight is optional — sit and pray instead, fully honored, no explanation owed
“The words get you to the gate; the silence is where He meets you.”

panel.label: PSALM 23:1–3
lines: “The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul.”

items.text: Same shape as last week — guided walk-through, about twelve to fifteen minutes, all of us together in this room
Read slowly, with longer quiet than last time — then five minutes with your journal
Then family clusters for sharing by invitation only — “Silence is a complete answer.”
“Father, You are the vinedresser. We are going back into the gardens You already know. Walk where You want to walk. Tend what You want to tend.”

slides.title: The Garden Exercise — Whole Room, then Family Clusters

items.text: Settle (2 min) — then, simply: “[Name] will read for us tonight.”
Guided walk-through, senior-led (12–15 min) — same protocol as Week 9, longer pauses; the card carries the room
The visible handoff — “[Name], the room is yours.” / “Thank you, [name]. That was well led.”
Silent journaling (5 min) — what was the same as last week, what was different
Sharing in family clusters (10–12 min) — by invitation only; a parent opens; silence is a complete answer
The bright line — the teen leads the walk-through; the adults hold the sharing and anything that surfaces
“What happened in your cluster stays in your cluster.”
One word each, when you’re ready — not what was said, but what you noticed; you can pass
“Deeper.” “Same.” “Tender.” “Quiet.” “Harder.” “Found.”
A parent offers the first word — each one received without commentary
“A garden visited twice is a garden being tended. Whatever He is doing in yours, He will keep doing it this week.”
Keep the garden rhythm — two returns this week, five to ten minutes each
“You know the way now — you don’t need the script.” Go back, walk a little, notice where He is
Journal each visit — even two sentences — “the garden speaks slowly, and the journal is how you hear it across weeks”
If a return surfaces something heavy — stop, open your eyes, come back another day; tell a trusted adult
Three visits drops to two on purpose — a rhythm that survives, not a sprint that impresses
